title: Conjecture 1.8
statement_text: For every graph $T$, family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$ such that no $F \in \mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, and $\epsilon > 0$, it is NP-hard to approximate $\mathrm{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ up to additive error of $n^{v(T)-\epsilon}$ for a given input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices.
context_text: For graphs $G$ and $T$ and a family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathrm{ex}(G,T,\mathcal{F})$ denotes the maximum number of copies of $T$ in a subgraph of $G$ that contains no copy of any $F\in\mathcal{F}$ ($\mathcal{F}$-free); $v(T)$ is the number of vertices of $T$, and for $G=K_n$, $T=K_2$ this is the classical Turán number. For a graph $T$, an $m$ blow-up of $T$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of $T$ by an independent set of size $m$ and each edge by a complete bipartite graph between the corresponding sets. The authors prove that for every fixed $T$, finite $\mathcal{F}$ and $\epsilon>0$ there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm approximating $\mathrm{ex}(G,T,\mathcal{F})$ within additive error $\epsilon n^{v(T)}$, generalising a result of Alon, Shapira and Sudakov for $T=K_2$. If some $F\in\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then $\mathrm{ex}(K_n,T,F)\le n^{v(T)-\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon=\epsilon(T,\mathcal{F})>0$, so $0$ is already an approximation within additive error $n^{v(T)-\epsilon}$; the conjecture asserts that outside this easy case no significantly better approximation than $\epsilon n^{v(T)}$ is possible in polynomial time. For $T=K_2$ this is the theorem of Alon, Shapira and Sudakov (NP-hardness of additive error $n^{2-\delta}$ when $\mathcal{F}$ contains no bipartite graph). The authors prove the case $T=K_m$, $\mathcal{F}=\{K_k\}$ with $k\ge m+2$, and show that for a 3-connected $T$ on $t$ vertices and a family of 3-connected graphs none of which is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, approximating within additive error $n^{t-2-\epsilon}$ is NP-hard. They also ask, as special cases, whether approximating $\mathrm{ex}(G,K_m,K_{m+1})$ within $n^{m-\epsilon}$ is NP-hard for every $m\ge2$ (known for $m=2,3$), and whether the same holds for $\mathrm{ex}(G,K_m,\mathcal{F})$ when every $F\in\mathcal{F}$ has chromatic number at least $m+2$.
paper_title: Additive Approximation of Generalized Turán Questions
